name: Lipaxe tagline
text: Grow. Stability. One pay for all.

title: Lipaxe connects digital payments with the tools merchants need to run daily b...

name: TextBox 9
text: Lipaxe connects digital payments with the tools merchants need to run daily business. The starting point is practical: make it easier to accept, track and reconcile payments.

name: TextBox 10
text: Our strategy is merchant-led: build places where payments are useful, then connect customer wallets, payment rails and merchant workflows.

name: TextBox 5
text: Customers move between cash, mobile money, banks and separate apps to complete everyday payments.

name: TextBox 12
text: Merchants often manage collection, sales records and reconciliation in disconnected tools.

name: TextBox 13
text: Cross-border use adds currency, provider, settlement and compliance friction.

name: TextBox 15
text: Wallets, payment links and QR acceptance meet customers where they pay.

name: TextBox 16
text: Orders, catalog, receipts and staff tools turn acceptance into a workflow.

name: TextBox 17
text: Provider events, ledger records and reconciliation support clear operations.

name: TextBox 19
text: Lipaxe is designed to connect consumer payment experiences to merchant operations, not add another isolated checkout.

name: TextBox 16
text: Balances, transfers and payment activity vary by market.

name: TextBox 17
text: KYB, staff, sales, receipts and settlement visibility.

name: TextBox 18
text: QR, payment links, hosted checkout and APIs.

name: TextBox 19
text: The product set is released by market and provider readiness; planned modules are not represented as generally available.
Product availability varies by country and provider. Do not describe roadmap modules as live unless confirmed.

name: TextBox 16
text: Lipaxe prioritizes the Democratic Republic of the Congo first, with merchant acceptance as the practical entry point. Initial segments to validate include retail and hospitality, education and health, and transport or event collections. Rwanda and Burundi are subsequent opportunities, subject to local legal review, reliable payment partners, settlement capability and pilot evidence. This is a market-entry strategy, not a market-size estimate.
Market sequence reflects the company’s stated DRC-first strategy. Rwanda and Burundi require local validation before commitment.

name: TextBox 8
text: Mobile money and bank transfer rails

name: TextBox 9
text: One merchant workflow across payment channels

name: TextBox 11
text: Payment, order and settlement context together

name: TextBox 16
text: Design acceptance around real sales, staff and customers.

name: TextBox 17
text: Track payment state, settlement and reconciliation.

name: TextBox 12
text: Product foundations are implemented across consumer, merchant and operations workstreams. The live scope and readiness must be confirmed against the current production environment.

name: TextBox 13
text: No verified figures for active users, GMV, revenue, signed partners or merchant pilots were supplied for this deck. We will publish metrics only after reconciliation.
No verified user, GMV, revenue, partner or merchant-pilot metrics were supplied. Add metrics only after source reconciliation.

name: TextBox 19
text: Confirm country scope, provider contracts, compliance responsibilities and settlement controls before public commitments.

name: TextBox 20
text: Run a controlled merchant pilot; measure successful payments, reconciliation, support load and repeat use.

name: TextBox 21
text: Expand only when legal, provider, liquidity and operational gates are met in each market.

name: TextBox 9
text: Funding should remove launch risks first: country legal review, provider integration, settlement and reconciliation controls, security testing, and merchant onboarding.

name: TextBox 10
text: Any fundraising amount, budget split or runway should be set from an approved operating plan. This deck intentionally does not invent funding percentages.

name: Priority description 1
text: Market-specific advice, licensing analysis and clear accountability

name: Priority description 2
text: Reliable integrations, reconciliation and liquidity operations

name: Priority description 3
text: Independent testing, monitoring and incident readiness

name: Priority description 4
text: Onboarding, training, support and measurable pilot outcomes
The reference deck included illustrative traction and use-of-funds graphics; these were replaced because no verified figures or approved budget were provided.

name: TextBox 27
text: Three-person founding team: product and technology leadership, operations, and partnerships. Additional executive and specialist roles will be appointed as the company grows.
Founding team names and roles follow the team image and roles supplied by the user. Confirm titles before external circulation.
